anomalies.observed: USB-C CC1 is connected to GND through C14, a 100 nF capacitor. The expected CC1 pull-down resistor R1 is absent; CC2, by contrast, has R7 = 5.1 kΩ to GND.
anomalies.expected: CC1 should have a 5.1 kΩ pull-down to GND, matching the specified USB-C sink configuration and the CC2 implementation.

evidence.quote: USB-C CC1/CC2 pins go through R1/R7 (5.1 kΩ each) to GND

anomalies.impact: A capacitor does not provide the required steady-state CC pull-down. USB-C source detection and VBUS provision may therefore fail when the plug orientation places CC1 as the active CC pin, making USB power availability orientation-dependent.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is present: CC1 uses a 100 nF capacitor to ground instead of the specified 5.1 kΩ sink pull-down resistor. This can prevent USB-C source detection in one plug orientation.
